title: Practice 4: Someone who does or is something

blocks.text: Sentences and their English: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR). Words, meanings and how each word is built: the English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.why: **американец** — америка́нец: male American (citizen, resident). Wiktionary: Аме́рика + -ец.
exercises.context: The English says which word it is.

exercises.why: **глупец** — глупец: fool, blockhead, turkey, gander, dummy, dunce, idiot.
exercises.context: The English says which word it is.

exercises.why: **писец** — (historical, or, dated) copyist, penman, scribe, scrivener, writer. Source: Wiktionary, «-ец» (https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/-ец#Russian).

exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
pairs: fool, blockhead, turkey, gander, dummy, dunce, idiot
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: кни́жник — (colloquial) bibliophile, book lover; дво́рник — janitor; америка́нец — male American (citizen, resident); глупец — fool, blockhead, turkey, gander, dummy, dunce, idiot.

exercises.q: Tom saw an old man begging on the street.
exercises.ru: Том увидел ___, просящего милостыню на улице.
exercises.why: **старца** — ста́рец: (bookish) old man, whitebeard; (christianity) monastic elder, starets. Wiktionary: ста́рый + -ец.
exercises.context: The English says which word it is.

exercises.q: Tom worked as a reader to the blind.
exercises.ru: Том работал в качестве ___ для слепых.
exercises.context: The English says which word it is.

exercises.why: **творец** — creator, maker. Source: Russian Wiktionary, «-ец», meaning 3 (https://ru.wiktionary.org/wiki/-ец).
